items.stem: Why is a vendor's own 'we tested it and it is safe' statement not third-party assurance?

options.text: It lacks independence; third-party assurance requires an independent party applying defined criteria
options.rationale: Correct: independence is what distinguishes third-party assurance.

options.text: Because vendors cannot test their own systems
options.rationale: Vendors can test; the point is independence for third-party assurance.

options.text: Because it was not written in a report
options.rationale: Format is not the deciding factor; independence is.
Testing is valid; the issue is who performs and attests to it.

items.explanation: Correct: independence is what distinguishes third-party assurance.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are essential before starting an AI red-team exercise? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Defined scope and rules of engagement
options.rationale: Correct: scope and rules of engagement are prerequisites.

options.text: An escalation and safety plan for harmful findings
options.rationale: Correct: a safety/escalation plan is essential.

options.text: A guarantee that no vulnerabilities will be found
options.rationale: No such guarantee is possible or desirable.

options.text: Permission to publish all findings publicly immediately
options.rationale: Immediate public disclosure is not a prerequisite and may be harmful.

items.explanation: Correct: scope and rules of engagement are prerequisites.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An auditor concludes 'controls are effective' but the only evidence is a screenshot of a policy document. What is the problem?

options.text: The evidence shows a control exists on paper, not that it operates effectively
options.rationale: Correct: existence of a document does not evidence operating effectiveness.
Screenshots can be evidence; the issue is it does not support operating effectiveness.

options.text: The conclusion needs to be longer
options.rationale: Length is not the issue; evidence sufficiency is.
Policies can be audited; operation must also be tested.

items.explanation: Correct: existence of a document does not evidence operating effectiveness.
